title: Untangle weight-format compatibility and separate tokenizer handshake
creator: Marisol Ortega
description:
Background: Over time the model ingest pipeline accumulated several compatibility shims that try to handle multiple legacy weight file layouts and an ad-hoc tokenizer handshake embedded in the loader. These shims increase startup latency, complicate kernel selection, and are a common source of subtle failures when loading cross-format checkpoints (sharded vs monolithic; byte-order/endianness metadata variations; legacy header variants).

Goal: Reduce model startup tail latency and failure surface by extracting a small, well-documented weight-adapter layer and moving tokenizer negotiation out of the loader hot path. The work should make it simpler to add future formats, enable a strict compatibility matrix for production models, and allow the runtime to make earlier kernel/quantization choices.

Scope:
- Introduce a dedicated Weight Adapter interface (stable ABI) to normalize incoming weight metadata into a canonical manifest used by the runtime.
- Remove inline tokenizer handshake from model loader; implement a lightweight Tokenizer Bridge that runs as a separate initialization stage and caches results per model-version.
- Implement an opt-in compatibility mode for legacy headers (configs) behind a config flag so we can measure and remove it after a deprecation window.
- Add unit and integration tests for the adapter surface and Tokenizer Bridge, including failure modes (partial shard availability, corrupt headers).
- Add instrumentation to measure model start time split (manifest parsing, weight mapping, tokenizer handshake, kernel selection).

Deliverables / milestones:
1) Design doc and compatibility matrix (Confluence: /display/INF/Weight+Adapter+Proposal) — due 2025-02-14.
2) Weight Adapter interface + integration tests — due 2025-02-24.
3) Tokenizer Bridge implementation + per-model cache + tests — due 2025-02-28.
4) Telemetry + perf benchmarks across popular model shapes (seq len 512/2048) — due 2025-03-03.
5) Canary rollout on dedicated infra + monitor for regressions — due 2025-03-07.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end model cold-start median reduced by >= 20% for target models and 95th percentile reduced by >= 10% in canary.
- No increase in model load failure rates in canary compared to baseline (<= 0.1% change).
- All legacy-format handling behind a feature flag and documented in the compatibility matrix.
- Tokenizer handshake runs independently and cached per pinned model-version; loader no longer issues tokenizer queries during hot-path token decoding.

Implementation plan:
- Week 1: Finalize adapter ABI and minimal fields (weight shards, dtype, quantization meta, physical placement hints). Add feature flag scaffold for legacy-compat.
- Week 2: Implement adapter and Tokenizer Bridge; add cross-format test fixtures (small models, sharded/monolithic).
- Week 3: Hook telemetry, run benchmarks, iterate on perf hotspots (JSON parsing, IO overlap).
- Rollout: Canary on one Dedicated pool with synthetic traffic and real workload replay. If OK, expand to Reserved capacity and then Hosted infra with throttled rollout.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Adapter ABI omissions cause regressions for a small fraction of internal models. Mitigation: start with permissive pass-through for unknown metadata and log samples; maintain compatibility-flagged adapter to fall back to old code path for problematic customers.
- Risk: Tokenizer Bridge cache introduces stale tokenizer configs after model re-version. Mitigation: include model-version in cache key and expose a cache invalidation API.
- Risk: Parsing overhead shifts cost from loader to adapter. Mitigation: use streaming parsing and pre-compiled binary manifests for high-throughput models.

Observability: Add spans and metric labels for stage durations (manifest_parse_ms, weight_map_ms, tokenizer_handshake_ms, kernel_select_ms). Add dashboard tile to runtime-1.20 perf board showing before/after comparisons and per-model breakdown.

Links and artifacts:
- Design draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/INF/Weight+Adapter+Proposal
- Test fixtures repo branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-fixtures/branch/weight-adapter-proof
- Proposed PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1167

Notes: This ticket intentionally separates concerns (format normalization vs tokenizer negotiation) so future work (lazy shard activation, prefetching) can hook into a stable adapter surface.
